question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's entrenched authority within the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced through loyal appointments across the Politburo, military, and security services, underpins trader consensus that he will remain in power through the end of 2026. With no designated successor and age norms largely set aside since the 2018 term-limit changes, recent leadership signaling—including 2026 policy addresses on economic planning—shows continued active governance without internal fractures or external pressures sufficient to prompt removal. The 21st Party Congress is scheduled for late 2027, aligning with expectations of a fourth term rather than abrupt exit. While near-certain pricing reflects this stability, low-probability shifts could still arise from sudden health developments, elite realignments, or acute crises testing institutional loyalty.
